courseTitle: 100 Days of Code: JavaScript Data Structures and Algorithms

cues.en: Now in this lecture we are going to learn how the arrays are stored in the memory in JavaScript.
When you create an array in JavaScript, the engine allocates memory for the array elements.
The amount of memory allocated depends on the data type and the number of the elements in the array.
The memory allocation is dynamic, which means that as you add or remove the elements, the JavaScript
engine may need to allocate more memory or reuse the memory.
JavaScript arrays are usually stored in contiguous block of memory, meaning that each element is stored
next to its adjacent element.
This allows fast access and iteration over the elements.
However, the actual layout may vary based on the JavaScript engine and the data type that is stored
in the array.
JavaScript arrays are dynamic, so so the size can change as you add and remove the elements, and when
the size of the array changes, the JavaScript engine may need to allocate more memory or release the
unused memory.
This dynamic memory allocation can sometimes lead to fragmentation, which may affect the performance.
However, modern JavaScript engines often optimize the array memory management to minimize the performance
impact.
In JavaScript, arrays are accessed using their indexes, which is zero based integer.
This helps JavaScript engine calculate the memory address of an element in JavaScript.
Multidimensional arrays are represented as arrays of arrays, which also known as nested arrays.
While JavaScript does not have native support for multidimensional arrays, like other programming languages,
you can achieve similar functionality using nested arrays.
When it comes to the memory allocation, multidimensional arrays in JavaScript are stored as separate
arrays, each having its own memory block.
From this example, you see that this multidimensional array are stored in the memory separately, so
each nested array is an individual object with its own memory block allocated in the heap.
The outer array holds the reference to the inner array, and this references point to the memory location
of inner arrays.
Inner arrays hold the actual values.
Each element within an inner array is stored in a contiguous block, just like a single dimensional
array.
The memory location of the inner arrays themselves may not be contiguous, which can lead to slower
access times compared to single dimensional arrays.
It's important to note that memory allocation and management details may vary depending on the JavaScript
engine used.
Modern JavaScript engines often optimize memory usage and array access to improve the performance,
so this is all for the memory allocation of arrays in JavaScript.
Now in the next lecture we are going to go ahead and create the array.
